thread:
sam: Quick check — I'm trying to land a terraform change that rotates a service-account token used by our GH Actions runners. After the change, CI started failing: GH Actions matrix jobs kick off Atlantis plan/apply in parallel and we're seeing apply conflicts + ArgoCD post-sync flapping. Anyone run into GH Actions + Atlantis causing an apply storm during token rotation? Logs/snippet below.

sam: ```
Run terraform apply -auto-approve
Error: Error applying plan:
  rpc error: code = Aborted desc = resource lock conflict: another apply in progress
...
ArgoCD: post-sync hook failed: failed to reconcile, resource not found (transient)
```

maya: Yea, seen similar when multiple matrix entries hit the same workspace at once. Two quick patterns we used: 1) serialize applies per workspace using a concurrency/group lock in GH Actions or an external queue; 2) add backoff/retry around atlantis apply and a global apply-parallelism limit in Atlantis.

luke: For GH Actions, concurrency cancels in-flight runs rather than queueing, so it doesn't help for queuing. We solved it by adding a tiny queuing service (SQS + lambda) that only lets 1 apply run at a time per TF workspace. Simpler workaround: a pre-step that waits on an S3 lock file. Example small script we use: 

```bash
# simple S3 lock wait
for i in {1..20}; do
  aws s3 cp s3://infra-locks/${{ matrix.workspace }} /tmp/lock && exit 1 || true
  sleep 5
done
# create lock
aws s3 cp - s3://infra-locks/${{ matrix.workspace }} <<<'locked'
```

jess: Also be careful during token rotation: new token may not be picked up by all runners immediately -> provider auth errors mid-apply. Staged rotation helped: 1) rotate and store new secret, 2) update repo secret via GH API in a deployment job, 3) wait for runners to pick it up (we poll SecretsManager / runner env), then trigger atlantis applies. We added a polling loop like: 

```bash
# wait for secret availability on runner
for i in $(seq 1 12); do
  aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id prod/infra-token && break
  sleep 10
done
```

maya: If you control Atlantis helm chart, you can also set values to limit concurrent applies: 

```yaml
# values.yaml
atlantis:
  server:
    env:
      ATLANTIS_PARALLEL_APPLIES: "1"  # serialize applies across the cluster
```

sam: Good tips. I don't love adding another queue service right now. Wondering if we can do something simpler with GH Actions + atlantis wrapper.

luke: Another trick: have GH Actions post a small PR comment or file to a tiny repo that acts as a queue (use github api to create a check or issue comment), then a single dispatcher workflow consumes and runs atlantis apply. It's hacky but no infra to manage.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: FYI there was a spike of atlantis apply failures at 2026-02-03T14:12Z, tagging @oncall-infra for context.

jess: Also verify provider auth TTLs. If the rotation shortens token lifetime, long-running plan/apply may start with a valid token and expire mid-run, causing partial state and flapping. We added a job timeout trimming and a pre-check that ensures token TTL > estimated run time.

sam: OK I'll try an interim approach: add a small S3-lock wait step as the simplest queuing mechanism + poll for secret propagation before triggering atlantis apply. I'll post the patch in a PR later today. Thanks! :thumbsup:

maya: ping me in the PR, I can review the apply-serialization bits.

luke: If you want, I can prototype a tiny dispatcher action that reads a queue file. Low effort.

sam: Assigned follow-ups: 1) add S3-lock wait + secret poll (sam) 2) review ATLANTIS_PARALLEL_APPLIES change (maya) 3) prototype dispatcher (luke)

jess: also added a quick checklist in the PR template reminder: rotate -> propagate -> verify -> apply.
